assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md shows Strategy: 'by-repository' and two Epics: Epic 1 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' (Tasks 1, 2, 3) and Epic 2 'TC-9006: trustify-ui' (Tasks 4, 5, 6). summary-comment.md confirms two Epic sections with task assignments.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epic table: Epic 1 Summary = 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', Epic 2 Summary = 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both follow the '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: Each task file contains a '## Parent Epic' section. Tasks 1, 2, 3, 7 (trustify-backend) have 'Parent Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend'. Tasks 4, 5, 6 (trustify-ui) have 'Parent Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. All assignments match the repository.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Hierarchy links section: 'Feature TC-9006 --[Incorporates]--> Epic "TC-9006: trustify-backend"' and 'Feature TC-9006 --[Incorporates]--> Epic "TC-9006: trustify-ui"' with explicit note '(Individual tasks are children of their respective Epic, NOT linked directly from Feature)'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Incorporates links go from Feature to Epics (not from Feature to individual Tasks).'

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are numbered 1, 2, 3 (and 7 for docs). Frontend tasks are numbered 4, 5, 6. Task 4 (frontend) depends on Tasks 1 and 2 (backend). Task 5 depends on Task 4. Task 6 depends on Tasks 4 and 5. All backend tasks have lower numbers than dependent frontend tasks.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Non-doc/non-testing tasks (1, 2, 4, 5, 6) all contain: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Modify and/or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Testing task 3 (remediation-integration-tests) contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation task 7 (documentation) contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. All required sections present for each category.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md: 'Issue type: Epic (hierarchyLevel 1)' and 'Epic parent: TC-9006 (Feature)'. summary-comment.md Epic Creation Details: 'Issue type: Epic (level-1 issue type, hierarchyLevel 1)' and 'Parent: TC-9006 (Feature issue key)'.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 task files contain a '## Repository' section with a single value: Tasks 1, 2, 3, 7 = 'trustify-backend'; Tasks 4, 5, 6 = 'trustify-ui'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 task files contain '## Target Branch' (all set to 'main'), '## Description', '## Acceptance Criteria' (with checkbox items), and '## Test Requirements' (with checkbox items).

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 tasks have corresponding digest files: task-1-digest.md (sha256-md:7b3c032fe4564e07837451004c6c747f6fade3da8405430a6888669de832ac2b), task-2-digest.md (sha256-md:8312e7446c24058ace34fd13da91d8a4019b8a1eb51e66d212aebdf6b7abd1f2), task-3-digest.md (sha256-md:54d741feaa8f90c58e46ea9f3368217cc696626ab8d442eccfec77c5601119e0), task-4-digest.md (sha256-md:b8083cf47388a9fdc599db8608ec17b4aaf42e559d2a81e8e172ea12ba058f51), task-5-digest.md (sha256-md:5ac97f5d1ffc3b560ce3e5a6badfa354b94525be2672849d426fe20a5391ab28), task-6-digest.md (sha256-md:08bf20bc5f1ae827a3c2fc3b5008c7c52dff5ac6611dee6314dd831dfe336c9d), task-7-digest.md (sha256-md:6a265cb44a92483d06b9348e708265feba4738924f9ea5260bff535f3452ecb6). All use sha256-md: prefix with 64 lowercase hex characters.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All tasks with Implementation Notes (1-6) include convention rationales in the prescribed format. Examples from task 1: 'Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/mod.rs` matching the convention's module structure scope.' and 'Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/endpoints/summary.rs` matching the convention's `.rs` handler file scope.' Each rationale names a specific file and scope. No 'Not applicable' annotations found in any task file. No free-form prose rationales found.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Field Inheritance: 'Priority: Major (inherited from Feature TC-9006, propagated to all Epics and Tasks)'. summary-comment.md Inherited Field Values: 'Priority: Major -- propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks. The Feature's priority is "Major" (not "Undefined"), so it is included in additional_fields on all created issues.' Task Creation Details: priority: {"name": "Major"}.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Field Inheritance: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from Feature TC-9006; no fixVersion scope setting in Jira Field Defaults — defaulting to "both", propagated to all Epics and Tasks)'. summary-comment.md: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 -- propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks. The Feature has a non-empty fixVersions array, and no fixVersion scope setting exists in Jira Field Defaults (defaulting to "both"), so fixVersions are propagated to tasks.' Task Creation Details: fixVersions: [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}].

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists with an 'Inherited Field Values' section stating: 'Priority: Major -- propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks' and 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 -- propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks'. impact-map.md also has a 'Field Inheritance' section with the same information.
